title: Extract a ring region as its own closed mesh: cut along the smooth ring splines, cap the holes, ready for mesh booleans
description:
User request 2026-10-03, follow-on to CRAW-32 (ring regions). The point of segmenting a mesh with rings is to take pieces out: select one or more regions and turn them into their own closed mesh, which can then be recombined with others through the mesh boolean / CSG packages.

Cut along the smooth rings, not the edge sets. CRAW-32 floods regions with each ring's snapped edge loop as walls; the extracted piece must instead be bounded by the smooth spline the user drew. Approach (research 2026-10-03, recommended of three): keep CRAW-32's edge-set flood for selection, and cut only at extraction time inside one new node (extract_region or similar), so selection ids, the source mesh and saved graphs stay untouched.
1. Keep the crossings: SurfaceSplineTracer.tracedRing() already produces a TracedSurfacePath whose points sit on mesh vertices or edge crossings (edgeId, fraction); SurfaceSpline keeps only the xyz polyline and the snapped loop. Persist the crossings on SurfaceSpline. Note emitLeaf gives each point the cubic's xyz but the geodesic's edge tag, so project each point onto its tagged edge.
2. On a copy of the mesh, split the crossed edges at those points (HalfEdgeMeshEngine.splitEdge; consecutive splits in one triangle produce the chord), with a snap tolerance for crossings near vertices (see quadlayout/embedding FaceChordWalk / SnappingCarve, MINIMUM_SEPARATION, for reference).
3. Faces whose parent no curve crossed keep their region; faces cut from crossed parents are re-flooded from neighbours with the chords as walls, so the band between the snapped loop and the spline is classified correctly.
4. Keep the selected regions (SeparateGeometryNode's attribute carry), cap every boundary loop, which is now the spline itself, with MeshHoleFiller (Liepa: minimum-area triangulation plus fairing), and check the result is a closed 2-manifold that the Manifold boolean backend (csg/ManifoldMeshBooleanBackend) accepts.
5. A UI path in the editing scene's region tool: extract the current selection into a new mesh (save it as a .dsl statement chain or export, decide which).

Risks: coincident or near-duplicate rings cutting the same faces (fertility's ring_02/ring_16 and ring_04/ring_17), triangle-only splitting, rings traced at a lower depth than the cut needs.

Bug 2026-10-03 (user F5, CRAW-37 entry on the fertility copy): after several extractions (E with growing selections, region_9 up to region_0_1_2_4_5_6_9, exports of 80 KB to 950 KB OBJs) and E back to the surface, plus menu scrolling, the JVM died with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError in HTTP-Dispatcher, Thread-2 and idle-timeout-task, then Killed. The launch had no -Xmx (default about a quarter of 14 GB) and the async profiler attached. The user suspects extracted meshes stay in memory after going back to the surface. Find what is retained (heap histogram before and after E/E cycles, and after scrolling the model menu), fix it at the root (release extraction meshes, overlay buffers and GL objects when leaving the extraction, and never keep more than the current one), and confirm memory stays flat over repeated cycles. Also move the OBJ export out of ixdar-app/tmp to the worktree-level tmp/ so it never appears in git status.
definition-of-done:
1. On fertility, extracting one region (for example an arm) gives a closed 2-manifold whose boundary before capping follows the smooth spline within the trace tolerance, not the snapped edge loop (measured maximum distance reported). 2. The capped mesh passes the Manifold backend's validity check and survives a union with another extracted region. 3. The source mesh and the region selection are unchanged afterwards. 4. Screenshots in tmp/ of the selection, the open cut and the capped result. 5. Build checkstyle-green.

6. Kept on purpose as the extraction's result and the acceptance numbers: RingRegionExtraction's public counts cutVertexCount, cutTriangleCount, crossingCount, insertedVertexCount, snappedCrossingCount, componentCount and openBoundaryEdgeCount (the cut surface and its report line), and RingRegionExtractionBenchmark's printed summary lines '[extract]', '[extract] near-duplicate rings', '[extract] region' and '[extract] union of regions', which are the fertility measurement the user reads.

7. Twenty E/E extraction cycles on fertility leave the live heap (after GC) within a small margin of the starting heap; the retained-object cause is named on the ticket. 8. Exports go to the repo-level tmp/ (gitignored).
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: a cylinder with two smooth rings off the edge lines; the extracted middle is closed and its cut boundary lies on the splines. 2. Unit test: a crossing near a vertex snaps rather than making a sliver. 3. F5 on fertility: extract a region and show it on its own.
changes-made: Verification 2026-10-03 (worktree craw-37, on master daaf8216). New RingRegionExtraction (data/) cuts a copy of the surface at every spline edge crossing (crossings within snap=0.05 of an edge end or each other merge, so no slivers), splits each face along its chords and triangulates the convex pieces, re-floods with the spline cuts as walls (each piece takes the region most of its area came from), keeps the selected pieces, caps them with MeshRepair's Liepa filler and asks the Manifold kernel (new MeshBooleanBackend.solidStatus). Node extract_ring_region (select terms as ring_regions); spline_ring now carries its SurfaceSpline in the _surface_splines slot. Region tool: E extracts the selection and shows it on its own, O toggles open cut / capped, E again returns; the piece is exported to ixdar-app/tmp/extracted/region_<ids>.obj and the equivalent extract_ring_region statement is logged (export, not .dsl: appending to the working .dsl would make the extract the graph's last statement and replace the surface the ring scene edits, and a selection must not write the curated ring file; the node is the live .dsl form). Fertility (RingRegionExtractionBenchmark, 13 rings, no near-duplicates within half a radius, no crossing cuts): arm region 2 (ring_05/ring_17) boundary to spline max 0.109 (0.050 mean edges) vs snapped loops 1.264 (0.573 mean edges), capped 2/2 loops, closed, Manifold NO_ERROR; region 4 (4 rings) 0.083 vs 1.351, 4/4 capped, NO_ERROR; union through mesh_boolean 14410 faces, NO_ERROR, volume 178090 from 33660 + 146109; source positions, faces and region labels unchanged. In the scene, arm region 9 (ring_10/ring_14): boundary 0.056 vs snapped 1.127, 2614 faces closed NO_ERROR. DSL union of the arm and region 5 via extract_ring_region + mesh_boolean: one shell, 0 boundary edges, Euler 2. Unit tests RingRegionExtractionTest (cylinder: closed middle on the splines, near-vertex crossing snaps, node pieces union) and full suite 367/367 green; wt done build and launch run green. Screenshots: tmp/craw37-selection.png, tmp/craw37-selection-same-view.png, tmp/craw37-open-cut.png, tmp/craw37-capped.png, tmp/craw37-montage.png, tmp/craw37-union-arm-shoulder.png.

OOM 2026-10-03, cause: not the extraction. MouseTrap.hyperStrings (a static list every HyperString.draw() appends to) was only reset by the base MouseTrap's mousePos/paintUpdate; OrbitMouseTrap overrides both and never reset it, so in every model scene the open model menu re-registered its HyperStrings each frame and they were kept until the JVM died. Histogram before the fix, menu open with the cursor still over it (fertility copy): HyperString 49 -> 2585 -> 12501 instances, HyperChar 17k -> 942k (151 MB), HashMap 1.9M (89 MB); live heap after GC 62 MB -> 332 MB within ~100 scroll events, 1.38 GB a few minutes later, at frame rate whether scrolling or idle. E/E cycles alone kept the heap flat (48.6 MB) and RSS flat; the region tool only ever held one extraction, but held it after going back to the surface.

Fix: SceneInputFrameUpdater.update resets MouseTrap.hyperStrings after the handlers' paintUpdate, so every trap (OrbitMouseTrap, Scene2DMousePanTrap, FlyCamMouseTrap included) keeps only the strings of the frame drawn last; menu clicks still work (Mesh Boolean menu 'U union' click ran the union). Shared with master. RingRegionTool.releaseExtraction() disposes the extracted runtime's GL buffers and drops the extraction on E back to the surface, on leaving the tool, on a region rebuild and before a new extraction, so at most the shown one is held. OBJ exports now go to <checkout>/tmp/extracted (AutomationPortFile.checkoutRoot), which tmp/* ignores; ixdar-app/tmp/extracted was ignored only through *.obj.

Verified: 20 E/E cycles on the fertility copy with selections growing to 4 regions, live heap after GC 36.15 MB at start, 35.85-36.26 MB after every cycle (cycle 20: 35.90 MB), RSS 597-747 MB without a trend; menu open and 100 scroll events plus idle: 41.7 -> 37.4 MB, 5 HyperStrings live. mvn test 374 run, 0 failures. Screenshots tmp/craw37-extract-after-oom-fix.png and tmp/craw37-back-to-surface.png; ixd wt done passed.
